author: Parsifal-2045
body:
#### PR description:

This is a follow-up to some CA irreproducibilities reported in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52171#issuecomment-6614984585.

This PR makes the CA output fully reproducible run-to-run on GPU (it already was on CPU). Most of the run-to-run instabilities were linked to warp-collective actions in the CA's duplicate removers, whose behaviour changed in alpaka 2.2.0. One example is the ` Kernel_fastDuplicateRemover`, which now gives heavy cells to a whole block instead of to a warp. The warp found these cells with `warp::ballot` and read them with `warp::shfl`, after code in which the lanes diverge. Since alpaka 2.2.0 these collectives use the mask of the lanes active at the call (`__activemask()`), so a lane could read another cell's index or track count and skip tracks. This is not the case anymore since no warp collective is used in the new implementation. I also took the occasion to improve the performance of these kernels, especially when dealing with "heavy" cells.

While this set of changes targets the run-to-run reproducibility, it also improves the CPU-to-GPU matching, and I've further improved the agreement between different backends with a change in the CA's fishbone.  This treated two cells as aligned if (d1d2)  t n1 n2, with t = 0.99999 or 0.999999 (basically a test on the cosine of the angle between the two segments). Values for this cut are extremely close to 1, and rounding results might differ between CPU and GPU.
   - The test is now |d1d2|  (1t) n1 n2, effectively the same cut keeping the floating point precision

#### PR validation:

This PR is purely technical. No significant changes are expected in physics performance. The code compiles and runs. The run-to-run irreproducibility was already <<1%, so it's quite difficult to show it in DQM plots (some repetitions for both the baseline extended PixelTracks and the vector-hits based tracks can be found [here](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/itaca/fixReproducibility/))

Tested locally on 300 QCD events (where the differences were more pronounced), run-to-run results are now fully reproducible on both CPU and GPU, and the CPU-to-GPU differences drop from ~3.5k over ~550k tracks (~0.68%) to ~2 differing tracks (~0.0004%) with all changes included in this PR.

Note that some minor differences might show up in Run 3 or other `TrackerTraits` topologies, since the fishbone and duplicate removers are shared across all CA implementations.
title: Make CA run-to-run reproducible on GPU and reduce CPU-to-GPU differences
